title: Visualizing with Grafana 📈
description: Build dashboards and set up alerts on top of your Prometheus data.

slides.title: Grafana – The Dashboard King 🎨
slides.content:
# Turn metrics into pictures

Grafana is the most popular open‑source visualization tool. It can:
- Query multiple data sources (Prometheus, Elasticsearch, InfluxDB, etc.)
- Create dashboards with graphs, gauges, heatmaps
- Set up alerts with notification channels (Slack, email, PagerDuty)
- Share dashboards across teams

If you installed `kube-prometheus-stack`, Grafana is already running.

slides.title: Accessing Grafana 🚪
slides.content:
## Default credentials

```bash
kubectl port-forward svc/prometheus-grafana -n monitoring 3000:80
```

Login with:
- Username: `admin`
- Password: Get from Secret:
```bash
kubectl get secret prometheus-grafana -n monitoring -o jsonpath="{.data.admin-password}" | base64 --decode
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

quizData.question: Which data source does Grafana typically use for Kubernetes metrics?
quizData.explanation: Prometheus is the standard backend for Grafana in Kubernetes environments.

slides.title: Built‑in Dashboards 🎁
slides.content:
## The kube‑prometheus‑stack comes with many

Navigate to Dashboards → Browse and explore:
- **Kubernetes / Compute Resources / Pod** – CPU, memory per Pod
- **Kubernetes / Networking / Pod** – network I/O
- **Kubernetes / API Server** – API request rates
- **Node Exporter / Nodes** – host‑level metrics

These dashboards are curated and ready‑to‑use.

slides.title: Creating a Custom Dashboard 🛠️
slides.content:
## Build your own view

1. Create a new dashboard (+, Dashboard).
2. Add a panel → choose Prometheus as data source.
3. Enter a PromQL query, e.g.:
   ```
   sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="default"}[5m])) by (pod)
   ```
4. Choose visualization type (graph, gauge, stat).
5. Save and share.

Grafana also supports variables (like `$namespace`) to make dashboards dynamic.

slides.title: Alerting in Grafana 🚨
slides.content:
## Proactive notifications

You can set alerts on any panel:
1. Edit panel → Alert tab.
2. Define condition (e.g., average CPU > 80% for 5 minutes).
3. Choose a notification channel (Slack, email, etc.).
4. Grafana will fire when the condition is met.

Alertmanager (part of Prometheus) can also handle alerts, but Grafana alerting is simpler for dashboard‑level alerts.

quizData.question: Where can you set up alerts based on a Grafana panel?
quizData.explanation: Grafana allows alerting directly from panels with conditions and thresholds.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Import dashboards from Grafana.com

Thousands of pre‑built dashboards are available. Go to Dashboards → Import → enter a dashboard ID (e.g., `315` for Kubernetes cluster monitoring).
